Plan a batch of questions and queue it. Returns 202 with the job the worker will run.

One batch at a time: while a job is still queued or running it is returned unchanged,
since a second plan made now would pick the same passages and pay for them twice.

patch.description:
Correct a question, or retire it from the library and put it back.

Key points are replaced as a whole, and every quote has to be in the passage it names, as
in generation; one that is not is refused with 422 and nothing changes. A new question
text is embedded again for the duplicate check. While the local embedding model is away
the old embedding is cleared instead, so the check passes over the question rather than
compare against words it no longer has. Each change is kept in the question's report with
what it replaced; a change to what the question already says is no change at all.

get.description: The topic map, the topics with the most passages behind them first.

post.description:
Answer a question, have the answer graded, and reschedule the question. Only questions
in the library can be answered: one that was rejected or retired is not there to practise.

get.description: The answers given to a question, newest first.

post.description:
Grade an attempt again, after a failed grade or with a changed grader. Every earlier
grade is kept. The first successful grade reschedules the question; later ones don't.

get.description: One attempt with every grade it was given.
The question to practise next, without its answer, and why it was picked.
XP, level, streak and coins, worked out from every graded answer.

The labyrinth on the dashboard: a room for each topic with questions in the library,
how well it is known and what is due in it, the passages between the rooms, today's
thread through them, and the Minotaur's room, the weakest.
The dashboard's charts: the latest scores, the days practised, and what comes due.

XpOut.title: XpOut
XpOut.description:
The XP an answer earned, part by part: ten times its score, five for answering, half
as much again for a question that was due, five inside an interview limit, and, on the
day's first answer, the streak's length that day, up to ten.
